award_description: RURAL AMERICAN COMMUNITIES FACE POPULATION LOSS, GROCERY STORE CLOSURES, INADEQUATE AND EXPENSIVE HEALTH AND ELDER CARE, LOSS OF ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY, UNEMPLOYMENT AND MORE. AND MANY RURAL YOUTH ARE NO LONGER INTERESTED IN PURSUING CAREERS ON THE FARMS THEY GREW UP ON. COOPERATIVES OFFER A PATHWAY FOR FARMERS, RANCHERS AND RURAL COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO WORK TOGETHER TO BUILD LOCAL ECONOMIES THAT ALLOW THEM TO THRIVE.THE COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT FOUNDATION AND OUR NINE CO-OP DEVELOPMENT PARTNERS WILL USE PAST AND NEW RESEARCH ON THE CO-OP MODEL TO IMPROVE ECONOMIC CONDITIONS IN RURAL AREAS BY: 1) PROVIDING TRAINING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO START, EXPAND, OR IMPROVE RURAL CO-OPS, WITH A FOCUS ON FOOD AND HOME CARE; 2) EQUIPPING THE RURAL WORKFORCE OF TODAY AND TOMORROW WITH SKILLS AND RESOURCES TO LAUNCH, MANAGE AND GOVERN COOPERATIVE BUSINESSES; AND 3) BUILDING THE CAPACITY OF CO-OP DEVELOPERS TO MEET RURAL NEEDS. OUR PROJECT WILL HELP RURAL RESIDENTS AND BUSINESSES BUILD THE FUTURE OF AGRICULTURE AND ENSURE ACCESS TO CRITICAL GOODS AND SERVICES IN AMERICA'S HEARTLAND.
business_types: NONPROFIT WITH 501C3 IRS STATUS (OTHER THAN AN INSTITUTION OF HIGHER EDUCATION)

award_description: RURAL COMMUNITIES HAVE SIGNIFICANT ECONOMIC ASSETS AND ENTREPRENEURIAL ENERGY, BUT THEY ALSO FACE UNIQUE OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES IN MAINTAINING ESSENTIAL SERVICES AND LOCAL BUSINESSES. THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES THESE CHALLENGES THROUGH COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT, BYHELPING RURAL COMMUNITIES CREATE AND STRENGTHEN BUSINESSES THAT ARE OWNED AND CONTROLLED BY THE PEOPLE WHO USE THEM. COOPERATIVES OFFER PARTICULAR ADVANTAGES FOR RURAL AREAS BECAUSE THEY KEEP OWNERSHIP LOCAL, PRIORITIZE COMMUNITY BENEFIT, AND CAN MAKE BUSINESSES VIABLE IN SMALLER MARKETS WHERE TRADITIONAL BUSINESSES MIGHT STRUGGLE.THE PROJECT WILL WORK ACROSS MINNESOTA, WISCONSIN, AND IOWA TO HELP RURAL COMMUNITIES DEVELOP GROCERY CO-OPS THAT ENSURE CONTINUED FOOD ACCESS, AGRICULTURAL CO-OPS THAT HELP FARMERS GET BETTER PRICES AND ACCESS NEW MARKETS, CHILDCARE CO-OPS THAT ADDRESS CRITICAL WORKFORCE NEEDS, AND WORKER CO-OP CONVERSIONS THAT PROVIDE A STRATEGY TO PRESERVE LOCAL BUSINESSES WHEN OWNERS RETIRE. THE WORK INVOLVES PROVIDING HANDS-ON TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE INCLUDING BUSINESS PLANNING, FEASIBILITY STUDIES, GOVERNANCE TRAINING, AND ONGOING SUPPORT TO HELP THESE COOPERATIVES SUCCEED.THROUGH A PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT SERVICES AND THE UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN CENTER FOR COOPERATIVES, THE PROJECT COMBINES DECADES OF EXPERIENCE WITH INNOVATIVE APPROACHES TO CREATE NEW MODELS THAT CAN BE REPLICATED NATIONALLY. THE PARTNERSHIP WILL DEVELOP AND TEST NEW APPROACHES, PARTICULARLY FOR EMPLOYER-LED CHILDCARE CO-OPS, WHILE DOCUMENTING WHAT WORKS SO OTHER COMMUNITIES CAN BENEFIT FROM THESE INNOVATIONS. THE ULTIMATE IMPACT WILL BE STRONGER RURAL ECONOMIES WITH LOCALLY-OWNED BUSINESSES THAT PROVIDE ESSENTIAL SERVICES, CREATE AND PRESERVE JOBS, AND HELP RURAL COMMUNITIES TO PROSPER. BY KEEPING BUSINESSES LOCALLY OWNED AND COMMUNITY-FOCUSED, COOPERATIVES HELP RURAL COMMUNITIES SUSTAIN THEIRECONOMIES. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO STRENGTHEN THE NATIONAL NETWORK OF ORGANIZATIONS THAT SUPPORT COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT, ENSURING THAT RURAL COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE COUNTRY HAVE ACCESS TO THE EXPERTISE AND RESOURCES NEEDED TO PURSUE COOPERATIVE SOLUTIONS TO THEIR ECONOMIC CHALLENGES.THIS WORK SUPPORTS BROADER NATIONAL PRIORITIES INCLUDING FOOD SECURITY, RURAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, AND ENSURING THAT ALL AMERICANS HAVE ACCESS TO ESSENTIAL SERVICES REGARDLESS OF WHERE THEY LIVE. SUCCESSFUL RURAL CO-OPS CONTRIBUTE TO A MORE DYNAMICAND RESILIENTECONOMY WHILE PRESERVING THE RURAL COMMUNITIES THAT ARE ESSENTIAL TO AMERICAN AGRICULTURE AND CULTURE.
business_types: NONPROFIT WITHOUT 501C3 IRS STATUS (OTHER THAN AN INSTITUTION OF HIGHER EDUCATION)

award_description: RURAL COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE NORTHEAST FACE SIGNIFICANT CHALLENGES IN SUSTAINING SMALL BUSINESSES, RETAINING QUALITY JOBS, AND MAINTAINING ESSENTIAL SERVICES SUCH AS CHILDCARE AND FOOD ACCESS. MANY SMALL BUSINESSES LACK SUCCESSION PLANS, LEADING TO CLOSURES THAT HARM LOCAL ECONOMIES AND COMMUNITY VITALITY. COOPERATIVE OWNERSHIP MODELS OFFER A PROVEN PATHWAY TO PRESERVE BUSINESSES, INCREASE JOB QUALITY, AND BUILD LOCALLY ROOTED WEALTH. EXPANDING ACCESS TO COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT IS NOT ONLY AN ECONOMIC ISSUE BUT ALSO A COMMUNITY ONE, AS LOCALLY OWNED ENTERPRISES ARE MORE LIKELY TO REINVEST IN THEIR REGIONS AND MEET PRESSING COMMUNITY NEEDS.THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE HANDS-ON TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, PRACTICAL TRAINING PROGRAMS, AND COORDINATED NETWORKS THAT BUILD THE SKILLS OF WORKERS, BUSINESS OWNERS, AND COMMUNITY LEADERS TO LAUNCH AND SUSTAIN COOPERATIVES. CDI AND ITS PARTNERS WILL SUPPORT COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT, TRAIN COOPERATIVE DEVELOPERS AND WORKER-OWNERS IN GOVERNANCE AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT, AND STRENGTHEN REGIONAL NETWORKS THAT SHARE TOOLS, BEST PRACTICES, AND PEER SUPPORT. BY EXPANDING KNOWLEDGE AND PRACTICAL CAPACITY, THESE EFFORTS WILL HELP PRESERVE SMALL BUSINESSES, CREATE AND RETAIN JOBS, AND SCALE INNOVATIVE COOPERATIVE MODELS IN CRITICAL SECTORS SUCH AS FOOD SYSTEMS AND CHILDCARE. THE LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO FOSTER RESILIENT, COMMUNITY-CENTERED ECONOMIES ACROSS THE NORTHEAST, ENSURING THAT RURAL COMMUNITIES NOT ONLY SURVIVE BUT THRIVE.
business_types: NONPROFIT WITH 501C3 IRS STATUS (OTHER THAN AN INSTITUTION OF HIGHER EDUCATION)

award_description: THE KEYSTONE DEVELOPMENT CENTER, A 501(C)3 NONPROFIT WHOSE MISSION IS TO SUSTAIN COMMUNITIES, ECONOMIES, AND RESOURCES THROUGH COOPERATIVELY OWNED BUSINESSES, AIMS TO MEET THE GOALS OF IMPROVING THE ECONOMIC CONDITION OF RURAL AREAS IN THE MID-ATLANTIC STATES OF PENNSYLVANIA, MARYLAND, WEST VIRGINIA, NEW JERSEY, AND DELAWARE. RURAL PRODUCERS ALSO FACE CHALLENGES ACCESSING MARKETS, DEVELOPING VALUE-ADDED OPPORTUNITIES, AND ACHIEVING THE SCALE NEEDED TO REMAIN PROFITABLE.THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES THE NEED TO BETTER UNDERSTAND AND APPLY COOPERATIVE AND MUTUALLY OWNED BUSINESS MODELS AS TOOLS FOR RESPONDING TO THESE CHALLENGES. VAADC WILL CONTRIBUTE PRODUCER AND AG,RICULTURAL EXPERTISE, VALUE-ADDED BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT, OPERATIONAL PLANNING, MARKET ANALYSIS, FUNDING STRATEGIES, AND CONNECTIONS TO REGIONAL FOOD-SYSTEM NETWORKS.
